answer: One applicant leases a copper assay bench at a foundry for 120 days, posts a 150 token deposit, pays 95 dollars. Each ingot gets a numbered punch stamp and a weigh-in while a neighbor signs the tally with a quill pen chained to the bench. The master checks the tally twice against the furnace pulse log of firing times and heat. A forged tally forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 benches freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 950,000 dollars, like stamping copper coins with a hammer that cracks after a hundred strikes. The forger keeps a bench earning nothing.
